citation_precision.definition: Cited quotes the checker confirmed on the cited page, out of every quote the agent cited while answering, including ones it later fixed. A quote on a scanned page counts only once it is confirmed against the page image.

answer_accuracy.definition: Answerable questions whose answer line states every expected value, each grade next to its own element, and every required caveat, with no number that its cited quotes don't contain, out of 8.

correct_refusals.definition: Unanswerable questions the agent refused, out of 4.

false_refusals.definition: Answerable or conflict questions the agent refused anyway, out of 11.

disagreements_flagged.definition: Conflict questions whose answer line states every side's value, with no number that its cited quotes don't contain, out of 3.

failure_counts.label: Number not backed by a claim
Refused when the answer was there
Answered when it should have refused
Hole not the one in the quoted row
Cited a page outside these reports

failure_counts_note: Checker counts cover every rejected claim in the run, field sessions and eval sessions. Answer counts cover the 15 eval answers.

summary_points.definition: Points a short evaluation of Iron Lake should make, written before the summary session ran, that the summary's own text states.

summary_sentences.definition: Sentences code kept, out of every sentence the summary session proposed. A sentence is kept only if every number in it is in what it cites and it cites every side of any disagreement it touches.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The checker ignores degree signs and private-use font glyphs, and the agent now reads page text with broken font glyphs mapped.
changes_after_first_eval.why: Some PDFs draw the degree sign with a Symbol-font character (U+F0B0). In run 1 the agent left it out every time it copied those coordinates, and the checker threw out 7 quotes that were really on the page.

changes_after_first_eval.what: Two intervals only count as the same interval if their depths also overlap.
changes_after_first_eval.why: In run 1, two different IL-22-015 intervals (74.88 to 75.52 m and 111.00 to 119.00 m) had the same rounded grades, so code grouped them and showed a false width disagreement.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The to minus from check allows for how precisely each number is written.
changes_after_first_eval.why: In run 1 it flagged 41800 p10, which rounds 318.25 to 342.29 m to 318.3 to 342.3 m and keeps 24.04 m. That is rounding, not a disagreement.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The rejection message for an interval without a hole ID, and rule 4 of the system prompt, now say how to quote it: from the row that names the hole down to the row in question.
changes_after_first_eval.why: In run 1 the checker rejected three intervals quoted without their hole ID and the agent didn't retry them.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The field instruction says to cover every report and every page that states something, not only every report.
changes_after_first_eval.why: In run 1 the 2022 drilling session claimed only the Table 3 rows and none of the same intervals as stated in the text, so code had nothing to compare them with.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The session turn cap went from 40 to 60 model turns.
changes_after_first_eval.why: With every page in scope, the longest field sessions needed more room. In run 1 the longest used 33.

changes_after_first_eval.what: The scorer no longer treats page, table or figure numbers in an answer line ("Table 3") as values that need a claim.
changes_after_first_eval.why: In run 1 it flagged the 3 in "Table 3" as a number not backed by a claim.

changes_after_first_eval.what: Gold answer for q05: added the 38640 title page (Au, Pt, Pd), and 'Au, Pt, Pd' counts as naming the platinum group metals.
changes_after_first_eval.why: Run 1's agent found the 38640 title form, which the gold had missed. Checked against the page image. The copper and gold expectations are unchanged.
